children: was named TD Cowen's best idea for 2027 as the firm raised its price target to $112 from $104, yet shares moved 0.69% lower to $98.79 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 17. Investing.com reported that TD Cowen kept its Buy rating and that the shares were trading near a 52-week high of $100.56 after a gain of about 45% this year.

TD Cowen expects international reach and the franchise bottling system to support about 5% organic sales growth, ahead of consumer packaged goods peers. Coca-Cola's latest third-quarter results back that up: organic revenue rose 7%, unit case volume grew 5%, the comparable operating margin widened to 32.9% from 31.9% and comparable EPS climbed 11% to $0.91. Management raised full-year guidance to at least 5% organic growth and at least 11% comparable EPS growth.

Volume rising 5% while price and mix added just 1% is higher-quality growth than the price-led gains of recent years. The new $112 target implies about 13% upside, but the shares already trade near 29 times earnings. GuruFocus gives Coca-Cola a GF Score of 70/100, pairing strong profitability with a mid-range balance sheet and weak momentum. Its GF Value of $75.87 sits about 23% below the close, so the shares carry a roughly 30% premium that GuruFocus rates modestly overvalued. The next test is February's fourth-quarter report, where 2027 guidance must confirm the 5% organic growth TD Cowen expects.

title: Coca-Cola Stocks Move Lower Even as TD Cowen Names It Top 2027 Pick
